official.title: Postdoctoral Researcher (HARARA Project): Urban Heat Experiences and Inclusive Climate Adaptation
official.description_text:
Why does heat affect people differently? Join the Horizon Europe HARARA project to explore the lived realities of urban heat and shape inclusive climate adaptation solutions.
Job description
This postdoctoral position is part of the HARARA project, a Horizon Europe Mission initiative funded by the European Commission. HARARA examines both the objective and subjective experiences of heat among migrantised communities in Antwerp and Rotterdam. The project brings together researchers from Erasmus University Rotterdam, the University of Antwerp, and Delft University of Technology, alongside civil society partners Empact vzw and Cultuurwerkplaats Tarwewijk, to develop a holistic understanding of the impacts of urban heat. By exploring how people experience, interpret, and respond to heat-related challenges, the consortium aims to contribute to the development of inclusive and effective climate adaptation solutions.
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will be primarily responsible for conducting a comparative analysis of heat impacts in Antwerp and Rotterdam. You will analyse and correlate objective measurements of indoor temperature and humidity with survey data on residents’ perceptions and experiences of heat, collected from 75 households in each city. In addition, you will map and assess existing inclusive local climate adaptation practices in both cities and contribute to the development and refinement of policy frameworks and community-based adaptation strategies in collaboration with the project’s civil society partners.
You will be based within the section of Environmental Technology and Design (ETD). ETD contributes to inter- and transdisciplinary, context-driven and problem/solution-focused research and education for the sake of a better environment. It involves a collaborative design and engineering approach, with social-and environmental-based methods and techniques as operative instruments, as well as the development and application of advanced urban data science and geospatial information technologies to support this primary aim. Research and education blend environmental technology, urban ecology, citizen participation and environmental behaviour at different scales. There is a strong emphasis on the interaction of these fields in terms of theories, methods and techniques, as well as their application via concepts, strategies and spatial interventions, as a significant part of ETD's research portfolio concerns applied science for and often with public and private partners.
Job requirements
We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with:
A PhD in a relevant discipline, such as urbanism, environmental sciences, public health, sociology, or a related field.
Experience with quantitative data analysis, including the analysis of survey data and environmental measurements, and proficiency in statistical software such as R, Python, SPSS, or Stata.
Affinity with issues of climate justice, social inclusion, migration, and/or community-based research.
Experience conducting comparative or mixed-methods research is an asset.
An interest in translating research findings into practical and policy-relevant recommendations.
Excellent writing and communication skills in English. Knowledge of Dutch is an advantage, given the collaboration with local partners and field sites in Antwerp and Rotterdam.
The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within an international and multidisciplinary consortium.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.
These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.
Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty Architecture & the Built Environment
The Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment has a leading role in education and research worldwide. The driving force behind the faculty’s success is its robust research profile combined with the energy and creativity of its student body and academic community. It is buzzing with energy, with four thousand people enthusiastically studying, working, designing, conducting research and acquiring and disseminating knowledge. Our faculty has a strong focus on 'design-oriented research’, which has given it a top position in world rankings.
Staff and students are working to improve the built environment with the help of a broad set of disciplines, including architectural design, urban planning, building technology, social sciences, process management, and geo-information science. The faculty works closely with other faculties, universities, private parties, and the public sector, and has an extensive network in the Netherlands as well as internationally.

Discount with health insurers on supplemental packages.
Flexible working week.
Every year, 232 leave hours (at 38 hours). You can also sell or buy additional leave hours via the individual choice budget.
Plenty of opportunities for education, training and courses.
Partially paid parental leave
Attention for working healthy and energetically with the vitality program.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in the HARARA project examining urban heat experiences and inclusive climate adaptation in Antwerp and Rotterdam. Involves comparative analysis of objective temperature/humidity measurements correlated with survey data on residents' perceptions, local adaptation practices assessment, and policy framework development.

thematic_fit.rationale: Moderate thematic distance with some resonance. Position addresses social-environmental justice, inclusion, and community-based adaptation—values aligned with human-centred design philosophy. However, core research focus is urban heat resilience and climate adaptation, not learning, spatial cognition, or collaborative immersive systems. Emphasis on migrantised communities' lived experiences and participatory approaches aligns with the researcher's human-centred ethos, but the substantive domain (climate adaptation, public health, urban environments) is different from immersive learning systems.

methodological_fit.rationale: Good methodological alignment. Position explicitly requires quantitative data analysis (survey data, environmental measurements), statistical software (R, Python, SPSS, Stata), and comparative mixed-methods research. Researcher has intermediate skills in quantitative research, user studies, and experimental design. Posting emphasizes 'translating research findings into practical and policy-relevant recommendations'—a design-science approach aligned with the researcher's methodology. However, position requires advanced statistical analysis (correlating measurement and survey data) and mixed-methods comparative analysis, which demand more sophisticated statistics than the researcher currently has (beginner-level).

growth_value.rationale: Significant growth potential in quantitative research methods and statistical analysis (R, Python, mixed-methods). Researcher would substantially advance from beginner to intermediate/advanced statistics—a stated capability gap. Would deepen experience with comparative research design and policy-relevant evaluation. However, growth would be in climate/social justice research, not in immersive systems, spatial cognition, eye-tracking, or advanced HCI evaluation. Valuable methodological growth but not directly aligned with target research trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is priority-2 institution. Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment is design-oriented with strong research reputation. HARARA is Horizon Europe funded (Mission initiative), providing excellent funding stability and international collaboration (Erasmus Rotterdam, University of Antwerp, civil society partners). Position emphasizes transdisciplinary collaboration and community-based research, which aligns with researcher's values. However, research group (Environmental Technology and Design, ETD) focuses on environmental technology, urban ecology, and sustainability—adjacent to design but not a hub for human-centred XR or immersive learning. Networking would build climate/urban design community, not primary HCI trajectory community.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in relevant discipline (urbanism, environmental sciences, public health, sociology, or related). Researcher has MSc in Creative Multimedia—discipline is adjacent (design, human-centred research) but not in listed fields. Eligibility depends on institutional interpretation of 'related field'—borderline but potentially acceptable given environmental and social research components

Posting requires 'proficiency in statistical software such as R, Python, SPSS, or Stata.' Researcher has beginner Python; would need to rapidly develop R and/or SPSS proficiency to be effective in data analysis role
Posting prefers 'experience conducting comparative or mixed-methods research'—researcher has user-study and experimental-design experience but limited evidence of large-scale comparative analysis
Knowledge of Dutch is listed as an advantage given collaboration with local partners in Antwerp and Rotterdam; researcher has no stated Dutch proficiency
risks: Credential mismatch: researcher's MSc is Creative Multimedia, not urbanism/environmental sciences/public health; may not meet eligibility threshold depending on evaluation

Statistical analysis gap is significant; posting requires correlating environmental measurements with survey data using advanced methods (mixed-effects modelling not yet in researcher's toolkit); steep learning curve required
Domain knowledge gap in urban heat, climate justice, and public health; researcher would need to acquire substantive context in climate adaptation literature
Shift from learning design and immersive systems to urban/environmental research; peripheral to stated target trajectory
16-month contract is relatively short; researcher may not have sufficient time to reach full productivity in new domain before contract ends
Research focus is environmental/social sciences, not human-centred XR or immersive systems; would not advance toward priority research communities
